claims.evidence: PRIDE protocol: all experiments in three biological replicates; light cells treated with L-OHP, heavy untreated, then mixed. Deposited raw names carry three replicate tags 080408/110408/180408 (20 files each); MaxQuant experimentalDesignTemplate defines exactly three experiments OxaPt_5xIC50_[080408], [110408], [180408] with fractions 1-20. One source per (arm, replicate mixture) = six physical cultures; no source name is reused.

claims.value: SILAC light = oxaliplatin (L-OHP); SILAC heavy = untreated, in all three replicates
claims.evidence: PRIDE sampleProcessingProtocol: "grown in ... 12C6 (light) or 13C6 (heavy) labeled arginine and lysine ... Light cell lines were diluted ... and treated with concentration of L-OHP 29.3 uM for 240 minutes. Following treatment, light and heavy cells were mixed in the same ratio." summary.txt: Multiplicity 2, Labels0 empty, Labels1 Arg6;Lys6 for all 60 runs. Data check (orient.py): replicate log2 H/L correlations 0.76-0.81 (same orientation in all three, no label swap); highest H/L (heavy>light) proteins are nucleolar/processome and centrosomal/G2-M proteins (UTP11L, WDR46, NSA2, GLTSCR2, RPL7L1, DDX56, UTP14A, RSL1D1, NOL7, CEP41, ASPM, MAD1L1, HOOK3), and RPL/RPS and UTP/NOP family medians are log2 H/L > 0 in all replicates. The abstract reports exactly these classes (centrosomal, RNA processing/processome, ribosomal) as DOWNregulated by oxaliplatin, so they are lower in the treated channel = light. Explicit label statement and data agree.

Three biological replicates (PRIDE protocol, abstract "3 biological replicates"); numbered 1..3 within each factor-value group, one number per independent culture (spec README.adoc:330, campaign rule 3). The pairing of light and heavy culture of the same mixture shares the number.

limitations: The publication (J Proteomics 2017, doi:10.1016/j.jprot.2017.05.005) is closed access (Unpaywall closed, no PMC copy); only its abstract was read. All methods come from the PRIDE protocol texts, the raw instrument method headers and the deposited MaxQuant output. Not bypassed.

Channel map comes from the PRIDE sampleProcessingProtocol ("Light cell lines ... treated with L-OHP"), confirmed by deposited ratios (heavy-enriched nucleolar/centrosomal proteins = the abstract's oxaliplatin-downregulated classes). The paper text was not available to cross-check a possible label swap in any single replicate; replicate H/L correlations (0.76-0.81, all positive) argue against one.

MS1 scan range: PRIDE protocol says 300.0-1950.0 m/z but the raw instrument method of three sampled files (one per replicate) says o(300.0-1700.0); the raw value is annotated. The other 57 raw files were not opened.

MaxQuant version: the PRIDE dataProcessingProtocol says v1.3.0.5, whereas the deposited parameters.txt says 1.4.1.2 and the fasta is uniprot_Human_20130904 (protocol: SwissProt downloaded 4.4.2013). The deposited search output is taken as the record of the search; this does not change any SDRF column.
Untreated (heavy) cells: the protocol does not say whether they were mock-treated or harvested at 240 min; characteristics[sampling time] and characteristics[dose] are not applicable for these rows.
characteristics[passage number] = not available: the five passages refer to label incorporation, not the passage number of the line.
